items.title: In Turkey, public funeral ceremonies honor fallen PKK fighters
items.description: Since August 21, the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) – currently engaged in negotiations with the Turkish state – has published a list of around 100 fighters killed in recent years. Public funeral ceremonies have been held throughout major cities, especially in the southeast.

items.title: Tuareg rebels free more Malian soldiers in prisoner swap, sources say
items.description: Tuareg rebels have freed about 60 Malian soldiers in exchange for one of their own leaders, security sources said.

items.title: Somali piracy surges as the impact of the US-Iran war ripples outwards
items.description: Two ships were seized within four days last week raising to at least 13 the number attacked since January.

items.title: DRC President Tshisekedi calls for national dialogue excluding M23 rebels
items.description: In the Democratic Republic of Congo, President Félix Tshisekedi calls for a national dialogue to ease tensions, while excluding M23 rebels from taking part, as the government plans to suspend 11 public universities in rebel-controlled areas. items.title: After 6 months of war, Iran's battered regime remains entrenched
items.description: Instead of collapsing, the Iranian regime has dug in its heels and taken an even harder line.

items.title: Kremlin Says Ukraine Peace Talks on ‘Deep Pause’
items.description: The New York Times reported that CIA Director John Ratcliffe visited Moscow this week to push the Kremlin towards a peace deal.

items.title: The man behind Srebrenica: Ratko Mladic dies at 84
items.description: For many, Ratko Mladic represented the horrors of the Bosnian War. He was convicted of genocide for the Srebrenica massacre and of other war crimes. Now he has died in detention at The Hague.

items.title: In Sudan’s civil war, both sides target journalists
items.description: Local journalists reporting on Sudan’s civil war and humanitarian crisis there are facing a campaign of intimidation by rival military forces.

items.title: Ukrainian Drone Spots SOS, Sparking 3-Day Rescue From Frontline Village
items.description: After a Ukrainian drone operator spotted an SOS sign outside a destroyed home in the Donetsk region, a three-day rescue mission was launched to save a couple who were the last remaining residents of their frontline village. items.title: Russia Preparing New Mobilization Wave of 600,000, Ukrainian Intelligence Says
items.description: Ukraine’s intelligence agencies say Russia is preparing a new mobilization wave that could bring 600,000 additional troops into the war effort across 2026–2027. Kyiv says Moscow is tightening recruitment and coercive measures as battlefield losses rise and contract recruitment slows.
